constraints.note: Right gripper descends from above onto the coin (stage00/t0001_00 -> t0001_50 wrist above, fingers pointing down; frames 25/38/50). Coin rests propped on a small transparent stand; a side approach would plow into stand/table, so the top_down elevation category is load-bearing. Approach azimuth around the coin's face axis is symmetry-free, but that is not what this constraint pins.

Pinch closes on the coin's exposed upper rim (stage00/t0001_50, t0002_00): the coin is propped tilted on a transparent stand, so only the raised top part is graspable; the realized hold leaves most of the disc protruding (stage01/t0002_75), which is what makes the later handover possible. 'rim' would have been the sharper token than 'top', but the region shown and required matches.

Coarse xy centering over the coin during descent is visible (frames 38/50), but the realized closing line is at the coin's RIM, not its center: post-grasp the coin protrudes nearly a full diameter from the fingertips (stage01/t0002_75). Exact gripper.center==coin.center is one sample of the equivalence class of feasible closing lines; the load-bearing content (land the pinch on the exposed top of the coin) is already carried by region_grasp + approach_direction.

acceptance.note: Stage end state visually confirmed: coin pinched at its upper rim and lifted, transparent stand left behind on the table (stage00/t0002_00, frame 50). Losing this hold = no coin in hand = task fails.

constraints.note: Left (receiving) gripper approaches the coin horizontally, anti-parallel to the right (holding) gripper, converging fingertip-to-fingertip (stage01/t0004_25; frames 88/106). Not a symmetry freebie: the giver's pose dictates the receive direction; a top_down receive would collide with the right gripper's tall fingertip triangles that bracket the coin.
Right gripper demonstrably holds the coin through the transport to the meeting point (stage01/t0002_75 coin at right fingertips in mid-air; frames 50/69/88). Dropping it ends the task.

The left closing line must land on the narrow exposed band of the coin between the right gripper's fingertips and the far rim: too far out = weak pinch/miss, too far in = collide with the holding fingers. Demo shows fingertip-to-fingertip precision converging on the coin (stage01/t0004_25 -> t0005_00, frames 106/125). Unlike stage 0, aiming at coin.center is functionally pinned here.

During the dual-arm handover the two grippers converge tip-to-tip while bodies/knuckles stay apart (stage01/t0004_25, t0005_00). Gripper-gripper collision at the meeting point would eject the coin; core for any handover.

acceptance.note: End state confirmed: at stage01/t0005_00 (frame 125) the coin sits in the LEFT fingertips and the right jaws are wide open, backing away. Correct postcondition for the handover stage.

missing.name: order
missing.note: The handover only works because the right gripper opens strictly AFTER the left has closed on the coin: at stage01/t0004_25 both grippers are engaged on the coin simultaneously, and only by t0005_00 is the right open. Reversed order drops the coin mid-air. No sequencing constraint was extracted anywhere for this stage.

constraints.note: After the regrasp the left gripper holds the coin by the rim with the far edge protruding free (stage02/t0005_00; frames 125/130/134), and this hold persists through alignment (coin sliver at fingertips, stage02/t0005_75). Functionally required for a slot task: fingers must stay clear of the slit and the free edge must lead. Also subsumes the in-hand 'carry' relation for this stage's transport segment.

The alignment target of this stage and a hard prerequisite of insertion; the demo establishes it, but only just past the stage boundary: at the cited frames 139/144 (stage02/t0005_56, t0005_75) the coin is still up-right of the slit, arriving; exact over-slot centering is first visible at stage03/t0005_94-t0006_12. Correct relation, boundary-late evidence -- gold tolerance must accept segmentation lag here.

Coin must be staged above the slot before descent; demo trajectory passes through exactly this state (achieved ~t5.9-6.0, stage03/t0005_94). Same caveat as center_align: at the cited frame 144 the coin is above the bank's head/ear region, not yet the slot -- the aligned state materializes ~0.2 s after the 5.75 s stage cut.

The slit opens upward out of the pig's back, so the slot must be approached top_down -- a lateral approach cannot enter it. Demo's final approach and descent are vertical (stage02/t0005_75 wrist pointed down; stage03/t0005_94 onward). Fixed by the slot geometry, hence core, not a free azimuth.

acceptance.note: Semantically the right postcondition for fine_alignment (coin poised over the slot). At the exact boundary frame 144 (stage02/t0005_75) the coin is near-above but visibly offset toward the ears; truly-above occurs ~0.2 s later (stage03/t0005_94). Accept with loose tolerance / boundary-lag note.

Right acceptance for an alignment stage: centered-over-slot is exactly what this stage must hand to insertion. Same boundary caveat as above -- realized centering is first visible at stage03/t0005_94-t0006_12, just past the 5.75 s cut.

missing.name: axis_parallel
missing.note: THE core alignment constraint of this task and it was never emitted: the coin's plane must be brought parallel to the slit's plane (equivalently coin face normal parallel to slot plane normal) before descent -- a thin slit admits the disc edge-first only. Demo shows the coin edge-on, elongated along the slit direction as it reaches the mouth (stage03/t0005_94, t0006_12). The extractor even carved both axes as holes (coin_normal_axis, slot_axis) in this very stage but never bound them into a constraint. Only the spin about the coin's own normal is symmetry-free; this constraint pins exactly the two non-symmetric orientation DoF.

constraints.note: Vertical top_down descent into the upward-opening slit, visually continuous across stage03/t0005_94 -> t0006_31 (frames 144/148/153). Dictated by slot geometry; violation = no entry.
Maintained over-the-slot relation during descent: coin directly over the slit mouth at stage03/t0005_94 and entering at t0006_12. Lateral drift while descending jams the coin against the back; core.

Coin center tracks the slot center through entry (stage03/t0006_12 coin at slit mouth center; t0006_31 mostly swallowed; frames 148/153/158). Required tolerance is slit-width tight; core during insertion.
The task goal itself: coin visibly passes into the slit (stage03/t0006_31 only a sliver left; t0006_50 coin gone from view inside the bank; frames 158/162).

acceptance.note: Correct and sufficient success check: by stage03/t0006_50 (and stage04/t0007_68) the coin is no longer visible anywhere -- swallowed by the bank -- and the gripper retracts empty past the empty slit.

True en route (frames 153/158, stage03/t0006_12-t0006_31) but not the operative postcondition: once the coin has passed through, centering is no longer observable or meaningful (coin invisible at frame 162), and success is fully captured by inside. A during-constraint duplicated into acceptance.

missing.name: axis_parallel
missing.note: Must be actively maintained during descent, not just pre-established: any plane twist while lowering wedges the disc at the mouth of a slit barely wider than the coin. Demo holds the coin edge-on along the slit through entry (stage03/t0006_12 -> t0006_31). Same unbound-holes story as stage 2 (coin_normal_axis / slot_axis carved, never constrained).

missing.name: clearance
missing.note: The bank is free-standing and light -- the right arm retracted at handover (stage02/t0005_38) and nothing braces the pig. The demo stops the fingertip pads at the back surface and lets the coin pass through (stage03/t0006_31 -> t0006_50); over-descent would topple or displace the bank and lose slot alignment. The insertion_depth hole (5/5 votes) shows the extractor sensed a depth limit but emitted no constraint bounding it. (Pig pose looks slightly disturbed by stage04/t0007_68 -- the margin was thin.)

missing.name: order
missing.note: Release must follow entry: the coin is still gripper-guided while entering (stage03/t0006_12, t0006_31) and only fully freed once inside (t0006_50); releasing while merely above the slot drops the coin flat onto the pig's back. Note stages.json even assigns eef_event 'release' to the cleanup stage -- the ordering is real in the trace but absent from the graph.
